meta.title: Bathtub Overflow Trip Lever: Verification Addendum
meta.as_of_note: Dates and status are as of 2026-11-06 (UTC). Web sources were read on this date unless the row says otherwise.
meta.status_line: Verification addendum to the overflow dashboard (session 56e0fb61). Research only: no provider is license-verified, no quote is verified, and no work is authorized.
meta.owner_note: This addendum sits beside the existing overflow pages. It adds official-source quotations and checks on the repo. Addresses, unit numbers, tenant details and owner identity are intentionally excluded. The site is public (GitHub Pages on a public repository).

headlines: Seven license records are now verified on the official CSLB site (status, classification, bond, workers comp). The other five shortlisted names have no license number on record here and remain UNVERIFIED. No job fit or quote is verified.

The three quotes are unverified. Their names match CSLB records, but the quotes do not show a license number, so the issuer is not confirmed. Amounts are as supplied and are not directly comparable, because the stated scopes differ.

Permit: sf.gov (checked this session) says you need a permit before cutting into or replacing pipes, particularly pipes covered by a wall. SF Plumbing Code §104.2 exempts only work that does not cut into or remove piping. The described scope appears to fall outside those exemptions. DBI must confirm in writing before work starts.
All-in-one (drywall plus plumbing) needs a licensing combination under CSLB rules: C-36 for plumbing, plus C-9 for drywall, or a B license that subcontracts or holds the right trade classification.

Drywall: of the verified records, only Rapid Flow and Manny's hold a B license, and none holds C-9 (drywall). Four are plumbing-only (C-36). An all-in-one provider needs C-9 or B, or a written drywall subcontract.
next_steps: Ask SF DBI in writing whether the described scope needs a permit. Start from the official DBI page and PermitSF portal.

Confirm the license number and status of each candidate on CSLB. Seven are already confirmed on the CSLB record (see the contractors page). Confirm the drywall classification or subcontract arrangement for any all-in-one candidate.
Request written scopes from two or three license-verified providers. Scopes should cover drywall access, restoration, who pulls any permit, and warranty.
Confirm the building type (single-family or not). The owner-builder permit path in §104.1.1 applies only to single-family dwellings.
Get legal advice on tenant access and notice before any work in an occupied unit. This was not researched on this site.

requirements.requirement: Repair the bathtub wastewater overflow trip lever, which the owner says sits in concealed plumbing behind a wall.
Access from above is preferred. Five or more licensed plumbers reportedly declined to remove the overflow from above without risk to the hidden plumbing.
Access from below is the alternative. The unit below is a storage unit and may need an opened drywall ceiling.
One provider for both drywall and plumbing (all-in-one).
Work done by a licensed plumber or licensed contractor.
Experience with delicate work in an occupied unit.
Permit status decided under San Francisco rules before any work starts.
Compare the three quotes on a like-for-like basis.
Every table row has an official source link. Values that cannot be confirmed are left blank and flagged, not inferred.
requirements.source_label: Process rule; applied in this build

permit_rules.rule: Emergency work: permit within one day
permit_rules.section: SF Plumbing Code §104.1 (second paragraph, as amended)
permit_rules.quote: Emergency work for the protection of life or limb, health, property and public welfare shall have a permit obtained within one day of commencing such work, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays.
permit_rules.implication: Applies to emergency work only. The brief does not describe an emergency. Whether any emergency condition exists is for the owner and DBI to decide.

permit_rules.quote: Repair of leaks not requiring cutting into or removing piping.
permit_rules.implication: The exemption is conditioned on no cutting into or removal of piping. Opening a wall or ceiling to reach the overflow does not clearly meet this condition.

permit_rules.rule: Exempt: unstopping traps, sewers, vents or waste pipes
permit_rules.quote: Unstopping of traps, sewers, vents or waste pipes not requiring cutting into or removal of traps or piping.
permit_rules.implication: Limited to unstopping. Replacing the waste and overflow assembly is not unstopping. This exemption does not appear to cover the described work.

permit_rules.rule: Exempt: faucets, angle stops, hose bibbs, roof drain
permit_rules.quote: Replacement, repair or maintenance of faucets, angle stops, hose bibbs or roof drain not requiring cutting into or removal of piping.
permit_rules.implication: Lists fixture types. A bathtub waste and overflow assembly is not named. Whether it counts as piping is a DBI determination. Treat it as permit-required until DBI confirms in writing.

permit_rules.quote: A permit for inspection of the proposed plumbing work set forth in the application will be issued to State-licensed contractors or to homeowners subject to the requirements of Section 104.1.1.
permit_rules.implication: Permits go to State-licensed contractors, or to owners under §104.1.1. The §104.1.1 owner path is limited to single-family dwellings. The brief does not say whether the building is single-family.

permit_rules.quote: If you file on or after January 1, 2026, you must use the 2025 California Codes and the 2025 San Francisco Code Amendments. There is no grace period.
permit_rules.implication: Any filing made now uses the 2025 SF Plumbing Code cited above.

permit_rules.quote: Starting September 14, 2026, most over-the-counter construction permits will be available exclusively on the PermitSF portal.
permit_rules.implication: Permit applications go through the PermitSF portal. The portal link on the DBI page was not opened for this build.

permit_rules.quote: CLOSED Veterans Day 11 NOV. Permit Services and inspections will resume operations on Thursday, November 12, 2026.
permit_rules.implication: Permit Services and inspections are closed on Wednesday 11 November 2026 and resume Thursday 12 November 2026. Plan calls accordingly.

permit_rules.rule: Permit needed before cutting into or replacing pipes
permit_rules.section: sf.gov: Apply for a plumbing and mechanical permit (Requirements)
permit_rules.quote: You need a permit before cutting into or replacing pipes, particularly pipes that will be covered by a wall or buried in the ground.
permit_rules.implication: Stated directly by DBI's own service page. The overflow work is behind a wall, so this sentence applies on its face.
permit_rules.source_label: sf.gov: Apply for a plumbing and mechanical permit

permit_rules.rule: Contractor license types that can apply for a plumbing permit
permit_rules.section: sf.gov: Apply for a plumbing and mechanical permit (Requirements)
permit_rules.quote: Contractors must hold a C4, C16, C20, C36, C54, B, or A license to apply for a plumbing or mechanical permit in general. Your permit scope may be further limited depending on your license type.
permit_rules.implication: A C-36 plumbing contractor, or a B holder within its scope, can apply. A license check (see licensing page) still applies.
permit_rules.source_label: sf.gov: Apply for a plumbing and mechanical permit

permit_rules.section: sf.gov: Apply for a plumbing and mechanical permit (Homeowners)
permit_rules.quote: Only property owners of stand-alone single-family dwellings (R-3 occupancy) may apply for a plumbing or mechanical permit to do the work themselves.
permit_rules.implication: Owner self-permit is limited to stand-alone single-family homes. Whether this unit qualifies is not stated in the brief.
permit_rules.source_label: sf.gov: Apply for a plumbing and mechanical permit (Homeowners)

permit_rules.rule: R-2 apartment owners: drywall versus plumbing
permit_rules.section: sf.gov: Apply for a kitchen or bath remodel permit (Special cases)
permit_rules.quote: For R-2 apartment buildings, property owners can apply to do the construction work themselves for sheetrock, drywall, or cabinetry. They must hire contractors to do any electrical or plumbing work.
permit_rules.implication: Under this sf.gov page, drywall can be applied for by an apartment owner, but plumbing must go to a contractor. This page is for kitchen and bath work; whether this scope fits is not confirmed.
permit_rules.source_label: sf.gov: Apply for a kitchen or bath remodel permit

permit_rules.rule: Kitchen or bath permit scope limit
permit_rules.section: sf.gov: Apply for a kitchen or bath remodel permit (What to know)
permit_rules.quote: Apply online to renovate or replace kitchen or bath fixtures in-kind, with no structural work.
permit_rules.implication: The online kitchen and bath permit is for in-kind work with no structural change. Opening a ceiling may take the job out of this path and into a building permit with plans. Confirm with DBI.
permit_rules.source_label: sf.gov: Apply for a kitchen or bath remodel permit

licensing_rules.quote: A plumbing contractor provides a means for a supply of safe water, ample in volume and of suitable temperature for the purpose intended and the proper disposal of fluid waste from the premises in all structures and fixed works.
licensing_rules.implication: Plumbing work of this kind needs a C-36 holder.

licensing_rules.quote: A drywall contractor lays out and installs gypsum wall board and gypsum wall board assemblies including nonstructural metal framing members, and performs the taping and texturing operations.
licensing_rules.implication: Drywall ceiling or wall work is a C-9 scope. Drywall can also be done under a B license if the rules in L3 are met.

licensing_rules.quote: A general building contractor shall not take a prime contract for any project involving trades other than framing or carpentry unless the prime contract requires at least two unrelated building trades or crafts other than framing or carpentry, or unless the general building contractor holds the appropriate license classification or subcontracts with an appropriately licensed specialty contractor to perform the work.
licensing_rules.implication: A B holder cannot take plumbing as a prime contract unless it holds C-36 or subcontracts a licensed C-36 contractor. This sets the licensing options for all-in-one.
licensing_rules.source_label: CSLB: B - General Building Contractor (Bus. & Prof. Code §7057(b))

licensing_rules.quote: Look up a contractor license or Home Improvement Salesperson (HIS) registration to verify information, including complaint disclosure.

flags.title: Permit status is open, and SF text suggests a permit is needed
flags.detail: The owner's brief says the work is to be done without a permit. The SF Plumbing Code exemptions (§104.2) cover only work that does not cut into or remove piping. Opening drywall and replacing the waste and overflow appears outside those exemptions. This project did not find a verified basis for doing the work without a permit, and it does not treat permit status as optional. The owner's private reasons for timing are not recorded here. The owner asked that permit-related information be left off the site. It is included because the official text bears directly on the scope. Decision and confirmation sit with SF DBI and the owner.
flags.owner_action: Ask SF DBI in writing whether the scope needs a permit. Take that answer to a licensed contractor before scheduling. Consider legal advice.

flags.title: Seven provider licenses are verified on CSLB; job fit and quotes are not
flags.detail: The CSLB record for each of the seven license numbers is cited on the contractors page. Those records show status, classification, bond and workers comp. They do not show job fit, insurance adequacy, or who issued any quote. Six other shortlisted names have no license number here and stay UNVERIFIED.
flags.owner_action: Ask each provider for a written quote that states its CSLB license number, address and scope, including drywall.

flags.title: Quotes are unverified and not like-for-like
flags.detail: The three quotes come from the owner. No provider address, license number or contact was supplied, and no provider could be matched to a listing with confidence. Quote dates: 8/30/26 is 68 days before 2026-11-06, and the other two are undated. The $135 quote covers a handle adjustment. The $550 quote covers a lever and diverter. The $614 quote covers replacing the waste and overflow. Verified amounts are left blank on purpose.
flags.owner_action: Ask each provider for a written, dated scope with license number, access method and what is included.
